run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-16T15:44:04Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend-proxy is explained by a chain that bottoms out at the single product-catalog pod. From 2026-11-16T15:44:04Z frontend-proxy's ERROR-status span rate left zero and rose to ~2.0-2.5 errors/s (5m rate) by 15:49-15:50; those errors are the Envoy `ingress` operation returning HTTP 504 after ~15s while its `router frontend egress` span carries error=true with http.status_code=0 (no response from upstream). Proxy access logs confirm `504 UT response_timeout` after 14 999-15 000 ms on GET /api/products/<id> and GET /api/recommendations, i.e. the routes that need product-catalog. The failing dependency call is product-catalog: checkout's oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct client spans fail with gRPC 14 and `error reading from server: read tcp 100.96.4.114:59432->100.64.188.136:8080: read: connection reset by peer`, where 100.64.188.136 is the product-catalog Service ClusterIP; frontend's grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct fails with `14 UNAVAILABLE: read ECONNRESET` after up to 225 s, and recommendation's /oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/ListProducts client span took 38.7 s while product-catalog's own server span for that call lasted 36 µs. Product-catalog's served-span rate fell from 10.79 spans/s at 15:26 to 0 at 15:54, and its container stopped writing logs after 15:49:17 (including its 10-second reload ticker, which also skipped 15:44:07-15:47:47), yet the pod is the only replica, Running and Ready with restartCount 0, ~12 MiB of a 30Mi limit, negligible CPU, and its node is not CPU saturated (all otel-demo pods there ~0.21 cores of 4). The internal reason the product-catalog process stops executing is not established: no error output could be confirmed, no OOM/eviction/backoff evidence exists, and change history is unavailable, so an application/runtime stall and a transport-level stall toward that pod remain separable-but-unproven candidates.

claims.text: frontend-proxy's ERROR-status span rate was 0 through 15:43:04 and became non-zero at 15:44:04 (0.50/s), peaking ~2.47/s at 15:49:04-15:50:04 and ~0.94/s at 15:56:34; the same series shows STATUS_CODE_UNSET traffic collapsing from ~20-25 spans/s to ~2-5 spans/s over the same period.

The only error-producing frontend-proxy operation is `ingress` (first non-zero 15:44:04, ~2.0/s at 15:50), while `router frontend egress` stays at 0 ERROR-status spans until 15:47:04 and then only ~0.04/s; error spans carry http.status_code=504 and otel.status_code=ERROR with 15 000 000 µs (15s) durations, and the paired egress span carries error="true" with http.status_code="0".

frontend-proxy access logs show `504 UT response_timeout` with upstream response times of 14999-15000 ms for `GET /api/products/6E92ZMYYFZ` and `GET /api/recommendations?productIds=OLJCESPC7Z`, while `POST /api/cart` and `GET /api/cart` on the same pod returned 200 via_upstream within 5-250 ms.

checkout's client spans to product-catalog fail with rpc.grpc.status_code=14 and otel.status_description `error reading from server: read tcp 100.96.4.114:59432->100.64.188.136:8080: read: connection reset by peer`, which propagates as `13 INTERNAL: failed to prepare order: failed to get product #...` in oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder and as HTTP 500 on frontend's `POST /api/checkout` / `executing api route (pages) /api/checkout`.

The address 100.64.188.136 in that reset is the ClusterIP of Service product-catalog (port 8080, selector opentelemetry.io/name=product-catalog) in namespace otel-demo; its Endpoints resolve to pod IP 100.96.4.247 on node i-0b2137ceca968ac10.

frontend's `grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct` spans fail with `14 UNAVAILABLE: read ECONNRESET` after ~225.7 s, making `GET /api/recommendations` return 500 after ~270 s; in the same traces recommendation's `/oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/ListProducts` client span took 38.69 s and returned grpc status 0, while product-catalog's own server span for that ListProducts call lasted 36-61 µs starting ~18.6 s after the client call began.

product-catalog's own served-span rate collapsed: `oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct` went from ~11.0 spans/s at 15:25:04 to 4.55 at 15:45:04, 0.71 at 15:47:04, 0.33 at 15:49:04, 0.066 at 15:51:04 and 0 from 15:53:04; the service total fell from 10.79 spans/s at 15:26:00 to 0 at 15:54:00. Its spans carry STATUS_CODE_UNSET, so product-catalog reports no ERROR-status spans of its own.

The product-catalog container's log output ends at 2026-11-16T15:49:17.521Z, including its periodic `Reloading Product Catalog... / Loaded 10 products` lines, which appear on a 10s cadence up to 15:49:17 but skipped the interval 15:44:07-15:47:46; request lines appear in bursts with identical timestamps (e.g. 7 `Product Found` at 15:47:46.3298s and 18 at 15:42:43.56s). All 15 721 lines read end at 15:49:17 with no lines after that point in the window.

product-catalog is owned by Deployment product-catalog -> ReplicaSet product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc (created 2026-11-16T15:06:11Z) -> Pod product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-7rqh9; the pod is the only replica, phase Running, all conditions True including Ready, restartCount 0, no lastState entry, container started 15:06:16Z, image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-product-catalog, podIP 100.96.4.247.

The product-catalog deployment configures one container with requests cpu 7m/memory 15Mi and limits cpu 15m/memory 30Mi, env GOMEMLIMIT=16MiB and PRODUCT_CATALOG_RELOAD_INTERVAL=10, and no readinessProbe, livenessProbe or startupProbe, so the pod's Ready=True does not depend on application health.

The product-catalog container is not resource-exhausted during the incident: memory working set stayed ~11.4-12.7 MiB of the 30Mi limit, CPU usage fell from ~0.0070 cores (15:25-15:39) to ~0.0002-0.0013 cores by 15:50-15:55, and its CFS throttled-period ratio fell from ~0.18 to ~0.02.

The node hosting product-catalog (i-0b2137ceca968ac10, 4 CPU allocatable, node conditions Ready with no MemoryPressure/DiskPressure/PIDPressure) is not CPU-saturated: at 15:50:00 summed container CPU for all otel-demo pods was ~0.21 cores, with product-catalog itself at 0.0013 cores.

Only frontend (0.86 error spans/s) and frontend-proxy (0.78 error spans/s) report ERROR-status spans at 15:56:00; product-catalog, checkout, cart, accounting, ad, payment, recommendation and fraud-detection report none, and frontend's error spans are `POST /api/checkout`, `executing api route (pages) /api/checkout` and `grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder` plus a few GET/POST.

The cart path through the same frontend-proxy, frontend, cart and valkey-cart pods stayed healthy in the same window: the proxy logged 200 via_upstream for POST/GET /api/cart in 5-250 ms at ~15:50, and cart spans in slow traces were 100-507 µs server-side with ~183-330 µs HGET, so the alert is not explained by frontend-proxy itself, by frontend entirely, or by cart.

Rejected: node-level CPU saturation starving product-catalog. Total container CPU across otel-demo pods was ~0.21 cores against 4 allocatable CPUs, the node reported Ready with no pressure conditions, and product-catalog's own CPU use was below its 15m limit.

Rejected: OOM kill or crash-loop of product-catalog. Working set was ~12 MiB of a 30Mi limit, restartCount is 0 with no lastState/last termination reason, container state is running since 15:06:16Z, and the pod's only events in 15:38-15:50 are Normal/Updated.

Rejected: a product-catalog rollout, reschedule or eviction causing the errors. There is exactly one ReplicaSet (product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc, created 15:06:11Z) owned by Deployment product-catalog, the pod name dates from 15:06:16Z with restartCount 0, and no replacement or eviction evidence appears for it.

Primary remaining hypothesis: the product-catalog container stops executing for multi-minute stretches and does not accept or complete work. Support: its served-span rate fell to 0, its own 10-second reload ticker logs skipped 15:44:07-15:47:46 and stopped after 15:49:17 while node and cgroup had spare CPU and memory, and callers queued and were then served in bursts with identical timestamps. The exact internal mechanism (runtime/GC stall, goroutine or lock stall, or a frozen container cgroup) is not proven.

Alternative hypothesis: the transport path to and from the product-catalog Service stalls and resets connections (gRPC 14, `read ECONNRESET`, `connection reset by peer` to ClusterIP 100.64.188.136) rather than the pod's process being stalled. Support: product-catalog server spans completed in 36-61 µs while the caller-observed call took 38.7 s, and even a caller on the same node (recommendation, i-0b2137ceca968ac10) saw that delay. It cannot be separated from the process-stall hypothesis with the evidence available; no packet, netfilter or Cilium metrics were queried.

Inspect the product-catalog container's process state directly (thread/goroutine dump, or kubectl debug/exec into product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-7rqh9) and read kubelet/containerd logs on node i-0b2137ceca968ac10 to decide between an application/runtime stall and a transport-level stall.

Add readiness/liveness probes to the product-catalog Deployment (none are configured today) so a non-serving pod is removed from Service endpoints instead of producing 15s proxy timeouts, and review its tight limits and GOMEMLIMIT (cpu limit 15m, memory limit 30Mi, GOMEMLIMIT=16MiB) for this single-replica workload.

gaps: The internal cause of the product-catalog stall is unknown: a filtered log query for err/fail/panic/fatal/warn/timeout/reset over 14:44:04-15:59:18 returned status no_data (9358a7bb-30bf-4543-9350-dca4a98589cd-t0:81671c2e-9d16-4fdc-b174-9dbe0e65aa40), so the absence of error, panic or warn output in that container's logs is unverified rather than established; container exec/process inspection, thread dumps and kubelet/containerd logs on node i-0b2137ceca968ac10 were not available.

No change_history integration is available, so I cannot tell whether product-catalog's limits (cpu 15m/memory 30Mi), GOMEMLIMIT=16MiB, missing probes, or any node/CNI setting changed shortly before 15:44; per-pod configuration is only observed as current state.

A namespace event query filtered for OOM/Evicted/BackOff/Failed/Killing/NodeNotReady returned status no_data (d3cb9bac-5ee7-4be8-a212-76de4220c2d8-t0:baafe7bb-208e-4c6c-b8de-5bda28fb0212), so absence of such events across otel-demo is unverified; only product-catalog's own Normal/Updated events (15:38-15:50) and its container status were citable.

frontend's container produced no readable log lines for 15:40-15:59 (9358a7bb-30bf-4543-9350-dca4a98589cd-t1:37dfa815-f8d2-4939-b113-5a021543ef4c, status no_data), so frontend-side logs could not corroborate the product-catalog calls; only its spans do.

No slow-span trace matched for service ad (bba67cdb-969f-4028-9834-c42497ec95de-t1:1191f501-c2df-4c13-8025-6e24f141c884) or for product-catalog GetProduct over 1s (1b3cff09-f301-43b6-b381-1e9b65fdf71d-t1:70e3517b-862e-44c1-a124-579d70fe602a), nor did a frontend rpc.grpc.status_code=14 tag search (3b307b93-9084-4b1b-bffc-af3e5abdc544-t0:28e4588f-1a24-4435-bc9c-02243a350529); rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count returned nothing (bba67cdb-969f-4028-9834-c42497ec95de-t0:c1c5711c-0e60-44de-a9cc-0d5f7d1ee951), so client-side RPC status metrics could not be used.

No rpc_server_duration_milliseconds_bucket series exists for product-catalog (2b777786-f694-42d8-bf14-1c9f7ecb7dee-t1:4d29c404-015b-447b-bb80-fad7044946c9, status no_data), so a latency baseline for product-catalog could not be built beyond span durations.

Trace evidence is a sampled Jaeger view (several searches reported incomplete) and span counts are not request counts; no exact failure rate or complete call graph for product-catalog callers can be computed, and the last trace data was captured around 15:51.

The alert annotation value (1.4222) was not reproduced exactly by my queries; the measured 5m ERROR span rate peaked at ~2.47/s for frontend-proxy, so the alert's own expression and window are not identical to mine.

Impact beyond the in-cluster request path (load-generator -> frontend-proxy -> frontend -> checkout/recommendation -> product-catalog) is unverified; no customer or downstream consequence was observed.
next_steps: Capture a stack trace or process state of the product-catalog container, and the kubelet/containerd messages on node i-0b2137ceca968ac10, to determine whether the process was blocked, GC-stalled or frozen during 15:44-15:59.
Pull node-level CPU, conntrack and Cilium drop metrics for i-0b2137ceca968ac10 outside this Prometheus snapshot to test the transport hypothesis.
Compare product-catalog's resource limits and GOMEMLIMIT with the project's reference manifest and add readiness/liveness probes before the next incident.
